items.label: Medium
items.text: End immediately after 8-13 paragraphs of varying length, not including any trackers or external HTML elements.

items.label: Long
items.text: Write at least 13 paragraphs with varying verbosity. Chapter-length.

items.label: Flexible
items.text: Flexible length with varying paragraphs and verbosity. Keep outputs concise during regular, character-driven scenes, and slow down to be descriptive when the situation calls for deep interiority between the environment and the characters. End immediately for director’s turn. Increase, decrease, or stagnate the pace as needed. Use the previous turns to inform how long the scene will be.

items.label: No set limit
items.text: Determine paragraphs needed for scene. Use as much it the scene demands.

items.label: Short
items.text: Tight. Every sentence carries its weight or gets cut. Dialogue-heavy scenes, quick exchanges, rapid back-and-forth. Don't pad. Don't describe the room if the room doesn't matter. Get in, deliver the beat, get out. Match {{user}}'s energy: if they wrote two lines, don't come back with a novel.

items.label: Medium
items.text: The sweet spot. Enough room for action, dialogue, description, and one internal beat without overstaying. Most scenes live here. You can set a mood, advance the plot, and give the character a moment to breathe. Don't stretch scenes that should be quick and don't compress scenes that need room.

items.label: Long
items.text: Big scenes. Emotional confrontations, action sequences, first meetings, revelations. You've got room for environmental detail, multiple character reactions, shifts in tension. Don't waste it on mundane transitions. Long responses earn their length through density, not padding. Every paragraph should justify its existence.

items.label: Adaptive
items.text: Let the scene decide. Quick dialogue exchange? Two paragraphs. Climactic confrontation? Eight. Quiet moment of reflection? Three. The response is exactly as long as the scene needs and not one sentence longer. Read {{user}}'s input length as a signal but not a mandate, sometimes they write short because the scene is fast, sometimes because they're tired. Match the SCENE's energy, not just theirs.
